Share demo recording and slide deck

action_items: Maya Chen - Send pricing + dedicated trial details - 2027-04-27
Diego Alvarez - Share sample tracing query set and quickstart script - 2027-04-28

summary: AE+SE walked Nimbus through the Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Focus was on debugging flows, correlating request IDs to traces, and demoing fallback/rollout behaviors. Nimbus raised latency and data residency concerns; next steps are security docs and a Dedicated trial.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-04-25 15:00 PT | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees listed above

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. quick intro, i'll pass to diego for the console walkthrough.
[00:12] Jared Collins: yep thanks, we got about an hour. i'm jared, engineering manager at nimbus. aisha will handle infra/security q's.
[00:18] Aisha Khan: hi all, quick note, we need to validate data residency and encryption in transit at rest, and how logs are stored.
[00:25] Diego Alvarez: great, thanks. starting off, i'll share my screen, going to open the console tracing view — apologies if auto captions are a little off.
[00:35] Diego Alvarez: ok so here we have the tracing dashboard, top left you can filter by model, route, and time windows. the trace list shows request id, latency, tokens, and an error badge. you can click into a trace to see the span timeline.
[00:52] Lina: oh that span view looks useful, can you jump to the raw request payload?
[00:58] Diego Alvarez: yes, the right pane has request logs and raw payloads. note: sensitive fields are masked depending on tenant policy. we also allow search by correlation id which ties the console trace to the request logging system.
[01:12] Samir Patel: correlation id — is that customer-provided or generated by redwood?
[01:17] Diego Alvarez: you can pass your correlation id in the x-correlation-id header or we auto-generate one. both will appear in the trace metadata.
[01:28] Jared Collins: about retention — how long do request logs live? we have strict retention for PII in eu.
[01:34] Priya Rao: good question. hosted default is 30 days for request logs, with configurable retention tiers. for Dedicated or Private deployments you control retention and can hook to your S3 or on-prem object store. we'll share the SOC2 section that outlines this.
[01:50] Aisha Khan: and encryption keys? we need KMS/HSM integration.
[01:54] Maya Chen: yes we support customer-managed keys (KMS) and HSM integrations for Private. Dedicated also supports KMS in most regions. we'll include the integration guide in the docs we send.
[02:06] Diego Alvarez: jumping back — here's an error example: this request timed out at token generation due to kv cache thrashing. notice the error analysis view groups similar errors and surfaces the top offending prompt sets.
[02:21] Jared Collins: can you show how we'd triage a persistent 99th percentile latency spike?
[02:26] Diego Alvarez: sure. step one is to filter traces by route and 95/99 latency. then expand the spans to find where time was spent — model inference vs network vs pre/post processing. you can then correlate with request logs to inspect input sizes and prompt patterns; we also show hardware metrics on dedicated pools if available.
[02:46] Samir Patel: what about fallback behavior — if a higher perf model is unavailable, can we route to a cheaper/quantized variant automatically?
[02:54] Priya Rao: yes, that's part of the smart routing features. you can define policy-based fallbacks in the deployment config. in the console demo i can show a live failover scenario.
[03:04] Diego Alvarez: i'll trigger a simulated backend failure. watch the trace — request gets rerouted to the fallback model, trace shows two spans (primary attempt then fallback) and the console marks the request with a policy event.
[03:20] Lina: i like the policy events. how would our SREs find the bulk of these events quickly?
[03:25] Diego Alvarez: we have saved queries and alerting rules; you can create an alert on policy fallback rates or error grouping and connect to PagerDuty.
[03:33] Jared Collins: can we export raw logs for offline analysis?
[03:36] Diego Alvarez: yes, exports to S3 (or GCS) are supported; for Private you can keep them in your VPC.
[03:42] Aisha Khan: question on PII masking — is masking done at ingest or at query time?
[03:47] Priya Rao: masking is configurable, but for hosted pipelines we mask at ingest prior to storage. in Dedicated/Private you can implement masking in your pipeline or enable Redwood's masking rules.
[03:58] Samir Patel: fine — show me an example debugging flow for a reranking pipeline that returned inconsistent results.
[04:03] Diego Alvarez: okay, i have a sample trace. first i show the request log: you'll see the input candidates and the reranker scores. expand the score spans to see which model produced which score and any confidence deltas. then use the trace to follow how the downstream post-processor normalized labels.
[04:23] Diego Alvarez: sometimes transcripts have bad punctuation, so i'll note — you might see slight mismatches in auto-captured metadata.
[04:30] Jared Collins: noted. can we link traces to our internal tracing system?
[04:34] Maya Chen: yes we provide tracing correlation hooks; you can forward select headers and include our trace id in your trace. there is a small SDK snippet for that.
[04:44] Lina: how does the console handle sampling — are we looking at every request?
[04:48] Priya Rao: by default we sample for the hosted tier to balance cost; you can request full traces for specific routes or during a POC. Dedicated and Private can be configured for full capture with retention policies.
[05:00] Jared Collins: okay cool. what's the expected latency added by trace capture?
[05:04] Diego Alvarez: negligible for metadata only — a few ms. full capture of payloads adds overhead depending on payload size; that's why the sampling and async export options exist.
[05:14] Samir Patel: any SOC2/ISO artifacts you can send?
[05:18] Maya Chen: yes, we'll send the security whitepaper and SOC2 summary as part of next steps.
[05:22] Diego Alvarez: now demoing error grouping: you can click an error cluster, see the top 20 exemplars, and open a facilitated issue with stack traces and request ids to hand to your devs.
[05:38] Aisha Khan: can we redact fields in the exported payload?
[05:42] Priya Rao: yes, redaction policies are applied at export time; we have allowlist/denylist rules.
[05:48] Diego Alvarez: showing request logs table: you can sort by latency, tokens, user id, and then click into the raw JSON. note sometimes the transcript auto-gen mislabels user names — that's expected in speech-to-text.
[06:03] Jared Collins: on quotas and rate-limiting, if we push large bursts what's the console view to debug throttling?
[06:10] Diego Alvarez: throttled requests are annotated in traces and request logs. we also surface rate limit headers in the raw response and the dashboard has a per-route rate chart.
[06:20] Lina: wish list — we need a way to correlate prompt evictions in KV cache to a spike in latency.
[06:26] Diego Alvarez: good request; our KV cache metrics are visible in the model pool metrics and we can add that to a saved dashboard.
[06:33] Jared Collins: any gotchas with private deployments? we may want an on-prem option for eu-pii.
[06:38] Maya Chen: Private supports on-prem with air-gapped options; there is more ops work but you get complete control on data residency and KMS. we'll coordinate with your infra team if you go that route.
[06:50] Samir Patel: what's the onboarding time for Dedicated trial?
[06:52] Maya Chen: typically 2-3 business days to provision a trial pool, then we run a short benchmark together.
[06:57] Diego Alvarez: quick note, i'll drop a sample tracing query set and a quickstart script in the follow-up.
[07:03] Jared Collins: sounds good. any final questions?
[07:06] Aisha Khan: please include encryption at rest details and data flow diagrams.
[07:09] Priya Rao: will do.
[07:11] Maya Chen: recap — we'll send security docs, trial details, and the recording. follow-up POC scoping next week. thanks everyone.

[52:00] End of recording.

Notes: transcript has typical ASR artifacts; speaker labels approximate.
